comments.body: Phase 1 confirmed root cause: tests/_isolation.py runs both `git rev-parse HEAD` (`head`) and `git status --porcelain` (`porcelain`) synchronously with no timeout. A deterministic blocking-git experiment through the real `pytest_sessionfinish` hook kept nested pytest alive after `[100%]`; a captured live stack ended in `subprocess.run/_communicate -> tests/_isolation.py:porcelain -> tests/conftest.py:pytest_sessionfinish`, ruling out a still-running test, fixture body, and terminal progress rendering. The same missing bound is reachable through `_no_repo_commits` before/after each unmarked test. 100 normal repo-root status probes were median 0.0143s, p95 0.0164s, max 0.0610s, rejecting normal repo cost as the cause and leaving >80x headroom for the approved 5-second watchdog. Historical inspection shows both unbounded probes were introduced together in d8b077451b; no later timeout was removed. Important repair constraint: `TimeoutExpired` subclasses the currently caught `SubprocessError`, so adding only `timeout=5` would silently return `None`; timeout must be separated and surface as an explicit isolation-infrastructure failure while ordinary non-repo/launch/nonzero failures keep returning `None`. Legitimacy: defect, because the signed plan requires the fixed watchdog and explicit timeout failure, and the guard contract says checkout mutation must fail loudly. Caller sweep found only `_no_repo_commits`, session start/finish hooks, and their tests; none behaviorally depends on indefinite waiting or swallowed timeouts.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Final rebar-debug repair report.

Problem — repo-isolation session hooks could keep pytest alive indefinitely after the test body completed when a read-only Git probe blocked.

Proven root cause — tests/_isolation.py invoked both `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` without a subprocess timeout; Phase 1 runtime instrumentation showed the process blocked in the real post-test hook boundary. Ordinary probe failures were intentionally collapsed to `None`, but a hung child never returned to that handler.

Proof — a PATH-injected Git shim blocked only the second real guard probe. Without the repair, both real hook-path tests exceeded their 12-second outer hang guard and failed; normal Git controls completed. This distinguishes the missing inner watchdog from test-body hangs or pytest teardown ordering.

Test — tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py drives `porcelain()` through `pytest_sessionfinish` and `head()` through the autouse commit guard. The final oracle was GREEN (11/11 focused tests). Exact-defect mutation removing both inner timeout arguments returned the two hook tests to RED (0 passed, 2 failed after their outer guards); restoring the repair returned them to GREEN (2/2). The intentional wall-clock ceiling is explicitly sanctioned as a hang guard, and scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py is GREEN.

Fix — both read-only Git probes now use the fixed five-second `GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` watchdog and explicitly re-raise `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, while preserving `None` for ordinary OSError/SubprocessError/non-repository failures.

Scope and safety — the change is confined to test infrastructure and its regression tests; production behavior and dependencies are unchanged. Existing assertions were strengthened, not weakened. Final validation: focused tests pass, `make lint` passes, `make typecheck` passes, wall-clock-assert gate passes, and `git diff --check` is clean.

Siblings — both live repo-isolation Git probe surfaces (`head` and `porcelain`) were fixed and exercised through their distinct real hook callers. No other subprocess probe exists in tests/_isolation.py. CLI/MCP/library parity is N/A because this is pytest-only infrastructure.

Residual risk and prevention — the outer 12-second subprocess ceiling remains only as a stuck-test fail-safe and is now annotated for the repository timing gate; accepted because it does not determine functional success.

Replication — the original blocked-second-probe scenario now terminates through the five-second inner watchdog with an explicit isolation-infrastructure failure rather than hanging pytest.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Phase 1 RCA amendment from the full-suite reproduction. The five-second watchdog itself is correct, but `tests/_isolation.py` dereferences `subprocess.run` during the autouse `_no_repo_commits` teardown. Three existing tests intentionally monkeypatch `run` on a production module's `subprocess` reference; because every reference points to the same imported subprocess module object and the guard teardown precedes monkeypatch restoration for these fixture graphs, the guard invokes the test double and raises `TimeoutExpired` against its own `git rev-parse HEAD`. Focused runtime proof: the three exact nodes each passed their call phase and errored only at teardown (3 passed, 3 errors), with the traceback entering the test-local fake from `_isolation.head`. This rules out a real hung Git process and proves test-double contamination of the safety guard. Defect legitimacy: the repository-isolation guard is a suite safety boundary and must observe the real checkout independently of the code-under-test's subprocess doubles; existing guard self-tests are the authority. Expected repair: bind the real runner at the guard boundary so later module monkeypatches cannot replace it, while retaining the explicit five-second timeout and real blocked-Git fail-closed behavior. Tests under `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock.py` and `tests/unit/test_store.py` are held-out RED oracles and must not be edited.

This prevents later monkeypatches of the shared subprocess module from contaminating autouse teardown while leaving the existing 5-second timeout and exception branches unchanged. Scratch proof: both probes ignored a post-import subprocess.run test double; actual blocking Git shims raised TimeoutExpired at 5.00s for both head and porcelain; non-repo, OSError, and CalledProcessError paths still returned None. File-scoped ruff check, ruff format --check, and mypy passed; git diff --check passed. A guessed tests/unit/test_isolation.py invocation was not a test failure—the path does not exist. Real blocked-Git negative controls plus the complete repo-isolation guard matrix pass (14 passed in 13.81s), proving genuine probe hangs still raise TimeoutExpired within the five-second watchdog. comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Patch-set 2 CI follow-up RCA: the canary test monkeypatches the shared time.sleep module. Under Ubuntu CI load, repo-isolation subprocess.run reached Popen._wait timeout backoff before fixture teardown, and subprocess internally called that patched sleep, causing the unrelated canary fixture to fail. A deterministic held-out regression closes the child capture pipes while leaving it alive, proving the exact Popen._wait -> time.sleep path. The repair captures the original sleep primitive and temporarily gives only subprocess internals a stable sleep namespace around each bounded Git probe, restoring shared state in finally while leaving the test monkeypatch untouched. RED on patch set 2; GREEN after repair; deleting the stable binding returns the oracle to RED. The affected isolation, canary, and subprocess-environment matrix passes 70 tests; make lint and make typecheck pass.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
While debugging grindable-deviant-angwantibo, a rival mechanism was falsified for that incident but exposed a separate deterministic liveness gap. tests/conftest.py calls tests/_isolation.py::porcelain during pytest_sessionfinish, after pytest has already printed the per-test `[100%]` progress boundary. `porcelain()` launches `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` with no timeout; the sibling `head()` probe is likewise unbounded.

## Runtime proof
A fake Git that blocked only the second repo-root status call reproduced the exact post-dot boundary. SIGUSR1 captured subprocess.run/_communicate -> tests/_isolation.py:59 porcelain -> tests/conftest.py:681 pytest_sessionfinish. This was not the grindable incident root cause: 100 natural status probes were median 0.0143s, p95 0.0164s, max 0.0610s, while the incident observed stack and discriminating A/B identified pytest numbered-temp cleanup.

## Plan
- Add a fixed 5-second local watchdog to the read-only repo-isolation Git probes. This is more than 80x the measured 0.0610s maximum and bounds a stuck local child without adding configuration surface.
- Preserve the existing `None` result for ordinary probe failures/non-repositories, but surface `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` as an explicit isolation-infrastructure failure so timeout can never appear clean.
- Exercise `porcelain()` through `pytest_sessionfinish` and `head()` through the autouse `_no_repo_commits` per-test commit-guard fixture using deterministic blocking Git shims.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A blocking repo-isolation Git probe cannot keep pytest alive beyond the documented fixed 5-second watchdog.
- [x] Timeout produces an explicit isolation-infrastructure failure, never `None`/clean success.
- [x] Real `pytest_sessionfinish` and autouse `_no_repo_commits` paths are covered with deterministic subprocess tests.
- [x] Normal repo-isolation behavior and the default unit suite remain green.
